title: Square a crooked cabinet door: turn its top cup hinge's side screw with a screwdriver until the gap is even
instruction: The left cabinet door hangs crooked. Use the screwdriver on its hinges to make the gap between the two doors even from top to bottom, 2 to 3 mm wide, then shut the door and let go.
context: Carpenters and maintenance workers adjust cabinet doors on cup hinges after every install and whenever a door drops out of line (O*NET 47-2031.01 Core: install 'hardware, using carpenters' hand or power tools'; 49-9071.00 Core: 'Adjust functional parts of devices or control instruments, using hand tools'). On a Blum CLIP top hinge the front screw on the hinge arm moves the door sideways at that hinge, so turning the top hinge's screw swings the door's top edge and squares the gap. The screw is reached only with the door open, and the gap shows only with the door shut, so the fitter opens the door, seats the screwdriver in the screw, turns it, shuts the door and looks.
setup: Frame: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top, mm. Two frameless cabinet boxes (18 mm white melamine board, each 300 wide x 300 deep x 450 high on a 30 mm plinth) stand side by side, fixed to the table, fronts at x 400, joined at y 0, open sides toward the robot. Each has a 19 mm full-overlay door, 298 x 448 mm, 1.9 kg, with a 12 mm bar pull (120 mm long, 30 mm off the face) near its free edge, hung on two Blum CLIP top 110-degree full-overlay hinges (71T3550) 80 mm from its top and bottom, on 0 mm mounting plates (173H7100) on the outer side panels. The right door is square, 2.5 mm from the left door. The left door starts shut, crooked: the gap between the doors is 1.7 mm at 20 mm below the top and 2.6 mm at 20 mm above the bottom. Each hinge arm has a side-adjust screw (front, 32 mm behind the cabinet front, PH2 cross recess, 9 mm head) and a depth screw (60 mm behind the front). A 150 mm PH2 screwdriver (75 mm red octagonal handle, 31 mm across the corners; 6 mm shaft, 75 mm; 0.15 kg) lies on an 18 x 60 x 106 mm post, handle end at (281, -171), pointing 65 degrees left of forward.
scoring: Shut: the left door within 2 degrees of closed. Gaps: the reveal between the two doors 20 mm below the top and 20 mm above the bottom. Released: every part of both grippers (fingers, pads, palm, housing) at least 30 mm from the cabinets, doors and screwdriver, the screwdriver's tip at least 20 mm from every screw, door and screwdriver still, for 1 s. 1.0: at the end, shut, released, both gaps 2.0 to 3.0 mm and within 0.5 mm of each other. 0.5: at the end, shut with those gaps, but not released. 0.25: at the end, the top hinge's side screw turned at least a quarter turn the right way (opening the gap at the top). Gate, any time, 0: a side screw forced half a turn past the end of its +-2 mm travel (the thread strips). Real trial: a feeler-gauge set in 0.1 mm steps at the two marked heights (read the thickest blade that slides in); evenness is the difference of the two readings; a paint mark on the screw head for the turn; the video for the release.
fidelity: One rigid door pivot on the hinge's 110-degree swing (held open above 25 degrees, spring-shut below). Declared screw rule: with the tip in the recess (within 2.5 mm, driver within 30 degrees of the screw axis) the driver's roll turns the head, 1 mm of hinge travel per turn (assumed); no turning torque. Demo's 90 N per finger is a simulated grip setting (sim slip at 35-40 N). Our estimate of real need: ~20 N per finger (0.3-0.5 N m turn, 20 N push, pad mu 0.8, 31 mm handle), within a YAM's ~40 N.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (one valid session, seed 1, 2,400 steps; the screw was never turned); demo: 1.0 (step 1113, 55.65 s).
